answer: A cedar supplier and a lagoon surveyor should earn governance weight from coin-days held in escrow. The contract tracks deposit IDs and their locked amounts over time, counting each deposit once per ballot. Delegation divides existing weight; withdrawal resets its age. An attacker can whisper through a thousand fresh keys, but it cannot multiply the history behind one deposit. More votes require more capital locked for longer. This limits cheap identity splitting while still favoring wealthy, patient holders.
